findings.detail: The question has the same problem as M2-S60-T1. Both describe text-reply JSON with syntax errors that a downstream system rejects. In both, the answer is to define an extraction tool whose input parameters are the schema and read the data from the tool_use block, so the same reasoning leads to the answer. Option B (parser retry loop on text replies) repeats M2-S60-T1's wrong option C. Option D (format normalization rules) repeats M3-S02-T2's normalization distractor. The wrong options therefore largely reuse earlier sets.

blind_answer.reason: Tool use with a JSON schema as the input parameters is the most reliable way to get schema-compliant structured output. It eliminates JSON syntax errors such as missing brackets and unescaped quotes. Few-shot examples, retries and normalization rules only reduce errors or react to them; they don't guarantee valid JSON.
